projects.title: Manpackable Transformable Surveillance Robot
projects.subtitle: Wheel-Track Transformable Surveillance Robot — single-actuator Modified Watt II six-bar linkage
projects.impact: Single-actuator wheel↔track transformation · patent in process · multi-award winner
projects.description: A compact, rugged, man-packable surveillance robot that transforms between wheel mode and track-belt mode using a single-actuator Modified Watt II six-bar linkage. Designed for search-and-rescue, reconnaissance, and disaster-response operations in confined or hazardous environments.
projects.long_description: Designed a compact, rugged, terrain-adaptive rescue robot with a transformable wheel-track mechanism using a single actuator (Modified Watt II six-bar linkage), enabling reliable traversal across diverse terrains. Intended for critical applications in search and rescue, reconnaissance, and disaster response, the robot is compact, lightweight, and optimised for rapid deployment in confined or hazardous environments. Validated dynamic system performance through motion and torque simulations in SolidWorks, MotionGen, MATLAB, and Abaqus (FEA). Integrated ROS2, ESP32-CAM, and sensors (IMU, DHT11) for real-time video streaming and remote control. Prototyping via additive manufacturing and sheet-metal fabrication. Designed using DFMA principles for ease of manufacturing and assembly.
features: Single-actuator Modified Watt II six-bar linkage for wheel↔track transformation
Designed for search-and-rescue, reconnaissance, and disaster response
Compact, lightweight, man-packable form factor
Real-time video streaming via ESP32-CAM with remote control over ROS2
Sensor suite: IMU + DHT11 environmental sensor
DFMA-driven design — additive manufacturing and sheet-metal fabrication
Validated via motion + torque simulations in SolidWorks, MotionGen, MATLAB, and Abaqus FEA

projects.title: Sub-20HP Autonomous Agricultural Rover
projects.subtitle: Founding-engineer-led farm automation platform
projects.impact: Full-stack robotics: mechanical → embedded → ROS2 → cloud
projects.description: Sub-20HP agricultural rover automating labour-intensive farming tasks. End-to-end ownership: mechanical design, ROS2 navigation stack (Nav2 + FAST-LIO2 + Isaac ROS VSLAM), STM32 firmware over CAN/RS485, Jetson-based perception, Docker-based simulation, web-based fleet management.
projects.long_description: Architecting and implementing the full robotics stack at Agmove Robotics. ROS2 (Humble/Jazzy) navigation stacks using GNSS RTK, IMU, camera, and odometry; Nav2 with Livox Mid-360, FAST-LIO2, and NVIDIA Isaac ROS VSLAM; reliable robot architecture with sensor-fusion obstacle detection, image-processing-based human follow, and vineyard row-following navigation. Cube Orange Plus with PX4/ArduPilot/MAVROS. STM32 firmware to interface motor drivers, linear actuators, and sensors via CAN, RS485, I2C. NVIDIA Jetson for sensor fusion and high-level decisions. Docker-based simulation and deployment workflows. Modular software pipelines connecting high-level ROS2 nodes with low-level embedded hardware via micro-ROS. Web interface for robot control with MQTT bridge (Mosquitto), full frontend/backend for fleet management and a robot cockpit / mission planner.
features: ROS2 Nav2 stack with FAST-LIO2 and NVIDIA Isaac ROS VSLAM on Livox Mid-360
GNSS RTK + IMU + camera + odometry sensor fusion
Vineyard row-following + image-based human-follow modes
STM32 firmware over CAN, RS485, I2C; micro-ROS bridge to high-level nodes
NVIDIA Jetson for perception and decision making
Docker-based Gazebo / Ignition simulation workflows
Web cockpit with MQTT bridge for fleet management

projects.title: Robocon 2024 — Harvest Day
projects.subtitle: Two collaborative robots for ball shooting and seedling placement
projects.impact: ₹70K total prize money · 3rd in league among 56 national teams
projects.description: Designed two collaborative robots for the 'Harvest Day' theme — a semi-autonomous robot for picking/shooting coloured balls and placing seedling-like poles, and a fully autonomous robot for ball detection and basket placement.
projects.long_description: Participated in Robocon 2024 under the 'Harvest Day' theme. Challenge involved designing two collaborative robots: a semi-autonomous robot that picked and shot coloured balls and placed seedling-like poles, and a fully autonomous robot that navigated the field, detected coloured balls, and placed them into matching baskets without any human intervention. Contributed to the mechanical design of custom shooting and seedling-handling mechanisms in Fusion 360 and SolidWorks; integrated IMUs, colour sensors, and proximity sensors. Developed autonomous navigation and control algorithms using ROS2, Gazebo, Python, and MATLAB; performed extensive simulation and testing for precise coordination. Led a group within the team.

projects.title: Robocon 2023 — Ring Toss
projects.subtitle: Two robots for ring shooting on poles using dual-roller mechanism
projects.impact: 5th all-India · 2nd at MATLAB Modelling Award · automated shooting via simulation-derived data
projects.description: Built two robots for the ring-toss-on-pole game. Finalised a dual-roller ring-shooting mechanism after iterative prototyping; one robot used mecanum wheels, the other omni wheels. Automated the shooting task in MATLAB using simulation-derived datasets.
projects.long_description: Participated in Robocon 2023 (ring toss in pole game). Brainstormed many mechanism concepts, prototyped the strongest candidates, then finalised a dual-roller ring-shooting mechanism for accuracy and precision. Used CNC machining, sheet-metal working, and 3D printing — and designed parts as per each manufacturing process. Designed an internal-gripper for picking ring stacks. One robot used mecanum wheels, the other omni wheels. Performed MATLAB and Simulink modelling of both robots — generated motion, tested shooting mechanisms for design validation, simulated base drives for path-planning, and integrated contact forces and other physical parameters so the simulation matched the real robot. Automated shooting in MATLAB: ran simulations to capture the ring's estimated trajectory, then used data analysis to choose input parameters that put the ring into the pole automatically based on its position and the detected pole position. Built laser-and-camera-based pole detection and top-most-ring colour detection via image processing. Built the control system in MATLAB; the robots were semi-autonomous. Team finished 5th all-India and 2nd at the MATLAB Modelling Award.
features: Dual-roller ring-shooting mechanism finalised after prototyping
Mecanum-wheel and omni-wheel base drives
Internal-gripper design for picking ring stacks
MATLAB/Simulink full robot modelling with contact forces
Automated shooting via simulation-derived parameter dataset
Laser + camera pole detection and ring-colour detection (image processing)
Multi-process manufacturing: CNC, sheet metal, 3D printing

projects.title: e-Yantra Robotics — Hologlyph Bots
projects.subtitle: Custom omni-wheel robots with overhead-camera vision feedback
projects.impact: 95% positioning accuracy via ArUco · 30% faster sim-to-hardware transition
projects.description: Designed and programmed three custom omni-wheel robots (continuous servo-driven, holonomic) tracked in real time by an overhead camera using ArUco markers. Used ROS2 + micro-ROS for multi-robot coordination and Gazebo 11 for simulation; visualised in RViz and Foxglove.
projects.long_description: Worked on the Hologlyph Bots theme of e-Yantra Robotics Competition (eYRC) 2023-24. Engineered and programmed a multi-robot system with omni-wheel robots for autonomous geoglyph creation, using continuous servo motors with overhead-camera feedback for precise control. Developed real-time localisation with ArUco marker detection and an overhead camera, achieving 95% accuracy in robot positioning and optimising task execution using ROS2 and micro-ROS. Designed and tested control algorithms in Gazebo, with system visualisation in RViz and Foxglove — reducing simulation-to-hardware transition time by 30% and ensuring faster, more reliable system performance. Significantly enhanced skills in real-time feedback systems, robot kinematics, control algorithms, and simulation-to-hardware integration. Successfully completed all online tasks, advancing just before the offline stage.

Overhead-camera-only localisation via ArUco markers (OpenCV) — 95% positioning accuracy
ROS2 multi-robot coordination + micro-ROS bridge to MCUs

projects.title: Pipe Inspection Robot (400–900 mm)
projects.subtitle: Variable-diameter inspection robot — IIT Roorkee research
projects.impact: Pipe diameters 400–900 mm · CFD-validated thrust design
projects.description: Versatile robotic system for navigation and inspection of pipelines with varying characteristics, diameters (400–900 mm), and fluid dynamics. Scissor-mechanism-based geometry adjustment with thruster-based propulsion.
projects.long_description: Researched many pipe-inspection-robot architectures, then designed a versatile system capable of seamless navigation and inspection of pipelines with varying characteristics, diameters (400–900 mm), and fluid dynamics. Conceptual design and analysis/simulation of a scissor-mechanism robotic module. Control system used Raspberry Pi as navigator, Xbox controller as remote operator; ArduSub + QGroundControl + BlueOS + Cockpit for vehicle setup, configuration, and navigation. Tried multiple actuator-control techniques including sign-magnitude PWM (Cytron driver), locked anti-phase PWM (brushed ESC), relays, and direct MOSFET drive. Tested individual and integrated components. Did MATLAB modelling and CFD analysis to optimise motion dynamics and thrust force requirements during design verification. Improved inspection efficiency and reduced manual intervention.
features: Scissor-mechanism diameter adjustment (400–900 mm)
Thruster, BLDC, and brushed-motor actuator integration
Raspberry Pi + ArduSub + QGroundControl + BlueOS stack
MATLAB modelling + CFD analysis for thrust optimisation
Multi-strategy motor-driver evaluation (PWM modes, relays, MOSFETs)

projects.long_description: Developed a gantry-based agricultural robotic system for farm coverage with strong use-case advantages over both traditional and other advanced systems. projects.title: Mobile Manipulator Motion Planning
projects.subtitle: MORPH-I pick & place · freelance (obotx, Poland)
projects.impact: OMPL pick-and-place for a mobile manipulator in MuJoCo — base, 8-DOF arm & 11-DOF gripper all motion-planned
projects.description: End-to-end autonomous pick & place for the MORPH-I mobile manipulator using OMPL motion planning in MuJoCo. Base navigation, arm grasp, and gripper open/close are each solved by OMPL with their own collision-aware state space — planned, not scripted.
projects.long_description: Freelance project (client in Poland, obotx). Built an end-to-end OMPL motion-planning pipeline for the MORPH-I mobile manipulator in MuJoCo: RRT-based (x, y, yaw) planning for the mecanum base, an 8-DOF parallel-manipulator planner with per-state MuJoCo collision checks for the arm grasp, and RRT-Connect over the 11-DOF gripper joint space. Whole-body motion economy (wrist to arm to base priority), closed-loop control (measured per-finger contact forces, position-feedback placement servo, base correction from the measured residual), and predictable, honest failure handling. One press runs the full cycle: drive to object, plan and execute the grasp, transport, place on the shelf slot, and return to HOME. Dockerised on Ubuntu 22.04.
features: OMPL RRT base navigation (x, y, yaw) for a mecanum mobile base
8-DOF arm grasp planner with per-state MuJoCo collision checks
RRT-Connect gripper (11-DOF) open/close trajectory planning
Closed-loop: contact-force grasp confirmation + position-feedback placement
Whole-body motion economy (wrist to arm to base) with clean failure handling
